items.title: Gucci names Park Bo-gum global brand face
items.summary: Jing Daily's intel dispatch confirms Gucci named Korean actor Park Bo-gum as a global brand face, framed as a move to strengthen the house's Asia-Pacific appeal under creative director Demna.

items.title: Gucci cuts prices, but will Chinese shoppers return?
items.summary: Jing Daily analysis of Gucci's price cuts on handbags and ready-to-wear in China (e.g., the Mercato small tote down about 22% and the Ophidia mini bucket bag down about 29%) following Q3 directly-operated store sales that fell 9% on weaker mainland China traffic.

items.title: Everyone in China recognizes Gucci. That's the problem
items.summary: Critical trade-press analysis arguing Gucci's brand recognition in China has outpaced its desirability, citing Gen-Z Chinese consumers describing recent designs as increasingly dull and saying they will not buy Gucci without a discount.

items.title: 구찌·에르메스 고전하는데…'코치'에 지갑 여는 젊은 소비자들
items.summary: Korean business-press piece reporting Kering (Gucci's parent) and Hermes are struggling amid slowing Chinese consumption and demand, while Coach's accessible pricing drew young Korean consumers away from Gucci-tier luxury fatigued by repeated price hikes.

items.title: 구찌와 머라이어 캐리가 완성한 눈부신 2026 홀리데이 풍경
items.summary: Vogue Korea covers Gucci's 2026 holiday gift campaign featuring Mariah Carey wearing pieces from the new Butterfly special collection, inspired by the iridescent colors of butterflies.

items.title: グッチ、マライア・キャリーを起用した新たなホリデーキャンペーンを発表
items.summary: Japanese trade outlet reports Gucci's new holiday campaign starring Mariah Carey, positioned around gift-giving themes for the season and winter travel/togetherness imagery.

items.title: グッチの新型バッグ「グッチ NY トートバッグ」が登場！伊勢丹新宿店で「GucciCore」ポップアップを開催
items.summary: Madame Figaro Japan covers a GucciCore pop-up at Isetan Shinjuku tied to the new Gucci NY Tote bag, referencing the house's 70-plus-year history with New York since its 1953 store opening there.

items.title: グッチの「底打ち」に、中国が待ったをかけた。仏高級ブランド株は11%沈む
items.summary: Business Insider Japan reports Kering shares fell around 11% after China's demand weakness undercut hopes that Gucci had bottomed out, deepening the broader luxury slowdown narrative.

items.title: 박보검 구찌 오늘자 얼굴...jpg
items.summary: Popular Korean fan community thread sharing photos of Park Bo-gum at LACMA's Art+Film Gala in his first public appearance as Gucci global ambassador; comments are largely positive, focused on his looks rather than the brand itself.

items.title: 古驰2026年降价40%还关店125家，GUCCI还值得买吗？
items.summary: Weibo consumer-guide style post (account '藏家视野') walking through Gucci's 2026 restructuring - up to 40% price cuts on core bags, a raised target of at least 125 net store closures, and whether the brand is still worth buying - part of a wider wave of similarly templated finance/collector accounts covering the same topic, so weighted as lower-confidence volume rather than an authoritative single voice.

items.title: 欧莱雅一脚踏入奢侈品美妆大门
items.summary: Xiaohongshu post discussing L'Oreal's deal to take over Kering Beauty's 50-year license (including Gucci Beauty/fragrance) from Coty after 2028, read by commenters mainly as a corporate-strategy curiosity rather than a product story.

items.title: 如何评价巴黎世家设计师Demna？
items.summary: Zhihu discussion thread on designer Demna (now Gucci creative director) remains active with new answers; commenters describe reactions to his appointment as split roughly evenly between excitement and skepticism, calling him divisive but commercially effective.

items.title: 당근에서 산 구찌 신발, 정품인데 왜 AS 안되지?
items.summary: Older but still-circulating Korean consumer-complaint piece describing a secondhand-market Gucci shoe buyer denied after-sales service despite authenticity, cited here for the still-active discourse around Gucci's unfriendly AS policy versus other luxury houses; flagged as older than ideal freshness window and kept only because today's searches surfaced no fresher AS story.

items.title: 一日连关两店，Gucci在中国"失宠"了吗？
items.summary: Chinese business-data outlet piece examining whether Gucci has fallen out of favor in China after closing two Shanghai stores (Raffles City and New World Daimaru) in a single day, leaving the city with only seven Gucci doors; retained as background for today's ongoing store-closure/price-cut narrative despite being older than ideal freshness window.
